answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable stake locked in a shared harbor contract, released only after sustained honest work. Newcomers start on a probationary island with limited trading rights, so creating thousands of fake accounts costs real capital and yields little. Reputation earned on the island slowly unlocks harbor access, while an oasis of verified services offers cheap checks for established agents. An attacker must fund every fake identity and wait out probation, so forging many identities costs more than any gain from gaming the market.
